newsitem.title: CHINA: China, HK in exercise to stem smuggling of people.
newsitem.headline: China, HK in exercise to stem smuggling of people.

text.p: An armada from Hong Kong and China engaged trawlers loaded with illegal immigrants on Friday, and thousands of Chinese police battled a mob trying to break through to the border -- but it was all pretend.

China and Hong Kong deployed more than 80 vessels in waters around the Hong Kong-China border in an unprecedented joint exercise to combat the smuggling of illegal immigrants, and more than 3,000 Chinese border police held an exercise on land.
The sea games in Dapeng Bay aimed to prepare border police from both sides to cope with the tide of Chinese sneaking into Hong Kong ahead of the British colony's July 1 return to China.
With Hong Kong in view on one side and China's Shenzhen city on the other, the two security forces jointly intercepted 21 fishing trawlers being used as simulated smuggling vessels.
Smugglers, or "snakeheads" as they are known locally, use fishing trawlers and open-top speedboats to ferry Chinese migrants across to Hong Kong at night.
At one high point of the exercise, Chinese police clambered on board a "smuggling" boat after firing several smoke flares on to the vessel.

Chen Shaoji, security chief of China's Guangdong province, said he was satisfied with the drill and was confident that no mainlander would dare steal into Hong Kong after seeing the exercise, expected to be broadcast on Chinese television.
"Our cooperation with Hong Kong is very good. But the drill is to see whether there are any problems we can improve upon," he told reporters after the exercise.
Hong Kong's long coastline and hundreds of small islands with potential hideaways has historically made it an ideal area for smuggling and piracy.
In the first four months of this year, 7,406 illegal migrants from China, including children, were arrested in border areas, against 23,180 for the whole of 1996.
Hong Kong becomes a Special Administrative Region of China on July 1 after more than 150 years as a British colony, but mainlanders will still need permission to enter the territory.
Illegal immigration has been fuelled by rumours in southern China that illegals will be granted amnesty after July 1.
Hong Kong regional Marine Police commander Anthony Ferrige told reporters there will be no change in the role of the territory's Marine Police after the handover.
"Marine Police will continue to operate inside Hong Kong waters, and Chinese police will act outside Hong Kong waters and in support of Hong Kong when requested," he said.
Later in Nantou, on the outskirts of Shenzhen, more than 3,000 police battled each other, as officers in uniform fended off hundreds of comrades pretending to be illegal immigrants.
Police, some in riot gear and combat fatigues, and armed with AK-47s and tear-gas launchers, warded off the mob as they tried to swarm into Hong Kong after the handover to China.
At one point, officers fired smoke canisters and used water cannons on "illegal immigrants" who hurled missiles at them.
Police also demonstrated their bomb-disposal skills by dealing with a suspected "bomb".
